Subservice Organizations
answer: Amazon Web Services (infrastructure hosting) and PropelAuth (authentication) are the two subservice organizations (sub-processors) that process customer data on behalf of Deal Intelligence; both are carved out and covered by Data Processing Agreements. GitHub, Google Workspace, Resend, and the self-hosted compliance platform support operations but are not subservice organizations. Customer-controlled integrations (Slack, Salesforce, HubSpot, Clay) are outside the system boundary.

question: Critical Vendors
answer: Amazon Web Services (hosting and storage), PropelAuth (authentication), GitHub (source control and GitHub Actions CI), Google Workspace (personnel email and single sign-on).

question: System Description
answer: The in-scope system is the Deal Intelligence platform in AWS us-east-1: Lambda functions and Fargate containers (ECS) for compute, DocumentDB (single serverless instance, storage replicated across three availability zones, KMS encryption, automated backups with 35-day point-in-time recovery), S3, CloudFront with AWS Shield Standard, EventBridge schedules, and a VPC with private subnets and no direct internet access to the database. Infrastructure is defined in CloudFormation via the Serverless Framework (stack di-backend-api-prod) and deployed by GitHub Actions from the dealintelligence/di-backend-api repository (pull request and CI status checks required on the protected main branch). Customer authentication is PropelAuth (JWT) with Google Workspace single sign-on, so customer MFA is inherited from Google Workspace; RBAC provides company- and user-level data isolation. Monitoring: CloudWatch (90-day log retention; alarms on API errors and latency), CloudTrail (7-year retention in S3), a scheduled configuration-check Lambda that runs monthly against a fixed checklist and posts a dated pass/fail record to the compliance platform, and an EventBridge rule that routes security-relevant CloudTrail events through the breach-detection Lambda to an SNS alert to the CEO in real time. The platform processes business contact information and competitor interaction data; active leads are retained 24 months and customer account data for the duration of the relationship plus 24 months. Subservice organizations: AWS and PropelAuth (carve-out). The compliance platform is self-hosted on AWS, holds compliance records only, and is outside the system boundary. Trust services categories: Security, Availability, Confidentiality.

question: Mission & Vision
answer: Give B2B revenue teams a verified, daily view of competitive activity at the accounts they care about, so they can win net-new deals, protect renewals and revive closed-lost opportunities with facts rather than inference.

question: Types of Services Provided
answer: Verified competitor activity events and competitor-customer lists delivered through a REST API, an MCP server for Claude and other AI clients, Clay enrichment, Salesforce and HubSpot CRM writes, Slack notifications, and webhooks. Events refresh daily, are named on both sides, and carry a confidence score of 0.95 or higher.

question: Company Background & Overview of Operations
answer: Deal Intelligence LLC (Delaware) operates a business-to-business market intelligence platform. It surfaces verified competitor activity for revenue teams: named buyers at a customer's target accounts who have accepted outreach from named competitors, plus verified competitor-customer lists derived from DNS, certificate, and SSO/tenant evidence. The company is fully remote with no physical office; all infrastructure runs on AWS in us-east-1. Internal roles are the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), who holds all production access, and the Go-to-Market Contractor, who has none.
